claim: Parkinson's disease (PD), Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD), Lewy body dementia (LBD), multiple system atrophy (MSA) and several rarer diseases are classified as 'synucleinopathies'.
source: Parkinson's disease (PD), Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD), Lewy body dementia (LBD), multiple system atrophy (MSA) and several rarer diseases are together classified as 'synucleinopathies', a class of common neurodegenerative diseases characterized by the pathogenic accumulation of the 140 amino acid protein, α-synuclein (α-syn) in a subset of neuronal and glial cells.
evidence: This is a definitional statement establishing the classification of diseases based on established medical knowledge.

claim: Synucleinopathies are characterized by the pathogenic accumulation of α-synuclein in neuronal and glial cells.
source: Parkinson's disease (PD), Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD), Lewy body dementia (LBD), multiple system atrophy (MSA) and several rarer diseases are together classified as 'synucleinopathies', a class of common neurodegenerative diseases characterized by the pathogenic accumulation of the 140 amino acid protein, α-synuclein (α-syn) in a subset of neuronal and glial cells.
evidence: This is a definitional characteristic of synucleinopathies based on established medical knowledge.

claim: α-synuclein is a 140 amino acid protein.
source: Parkinson's disease (PD), Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD), Lewy body dementia (LBD), multiple system atrophy (MSA) and several rarer diseases are together classified as 'synucleinopathies', a class of common neurodegenerative diseases characterized by the pathogenic accumulation of the 140 amino acid protein, α-synuclein (α-syn) in a subset of neuronal and glial cells.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the protein structure based on established knowledge.

claim: Multiplications and missense mutations in SNCA cause familial, early-onset PD and LBD.
source: A causative link between α-syn amyloid formation and disease is supported by the findings that multiplications and missense mutations in SNCA, the α-syn gene, cause familial, early-onset PD and LBD (Goedert et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Goedert et al., 2013.

claim: The fibril core of α-synuclein is composed of residues 30–100.
source: Limited proteolysis and NMR studies suggest that the fibril core is composed of residues 30–100 (Miake et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Miake et al., 2002.

claim: Solid state NMR and cryo-EM studies revealed a Greek key-shaped α-syn topology in a compact domain extending from residue 44 to residue 97.
source: A solid state NMR (ssNMR) and recent cryo-EM studies of recombinant α-syn fibrils revealed a Greek key-shaped α-syn topology in a compact domain extending from residue 44 to residue 97 (Tuttle et al., 2016; Guerrero-Ferreira et al., 2018; Li et al., 2018a; Li et al., 2018b).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to structural studies.

claim: NACore comprises residues 68–78 of α-synuclein.
source: One segment is residues 68–78 termed NACore, which earlier work (Giasson et al., 2001; Periquet et al., 2007) had suggested is critical for α-syn aggregation and pathology.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about the NACore segment.

claim: NACore is critical for α-syn aggregation and pathology.
source: One segment is residues 68–78 termed NACore, which earlier work (Giasson et al., 2001; Periquet et al., 2007) had suggested is critical for α-syn aggregation and pathology.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Giasson et al., 2001 and Periquet et al., 2007.

claim: β-synuclein does not contain residues 73–83 and is not found in amyloid deposits.
source: Also, β-synuclein, a homolog does not contain residues 73–83 and is not found in amyloid deposits, and removal of α-syn residues 71–82 that encompass NACore has been shown to reduce the aggregation and toxicity in vitro and in a Drosophila model (Giasson et al., 2001; Periquet et al., 2007; Rivers et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Removal of α-syn residues 71–82 reduces aggregation and toxicity in vitro and in a Drosophila model.
source: Also, β-synuclein, a homolog does not contain residues 73–83 and is not found in amyloid deposits, and removal of α-syn residues 71–82 that encompass NACore has been shown to reduce the aggregation and toxicity in vitro and in a Drosophila model (Giasson et al., 2001; Periquet et al., 2007; Rivers et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Giasson et al., 2001; Periquet et al., 2007; Rivers et al., 2008.

claim: Modification at Thr72 reduces the aggregation propensity of α-syn.
source: Additionally, a modification at Thr72 reduces the aggregation propensity of α-syn (Marotta et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Marotta et al., 2015.

claim: NACore and residues 47–56 reveal amyloid protofilaments composed of dual β-sheet homo-steric zippers.
source: The other segment comprises of residues 47–56 and its atomic structure was solved by electron diffraction (Rodriguez et al., 2015). Both segments reveal amyloid protofilaments composed of dual β-sheet homo-steric zippers.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Rodriguez et al., 2015 and describes structural findings.

claim: α-syn fibrils vary in morphology and cytotoxicity.
source: The crystallographic homo-zippers and the hetero-zippers of the longer cryoEM and ssNMR structures are not necessarily contradictory; they may reveal information about different α-syn polymorphs, consistent with biochemical data that show α-syn fibrils, which vary in morphology and cytotoxicity (Peelaerts et al., 2015; Bousset et al., 2013; Heise et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Peelaerts et al., 2015; Bousset et al., 2013; Heise et al., 2005.

claim: Small amounts of α-syn aggregates can act as seeds and induce aggregation of native protein.
source: Staging of Lewy pathology has shown that pathology spreads over time through connected brain regions, and experimental studies have shown that small amounts of α-syn aggregates can act as seeds and induce the aggregation of the native protein (Braak and Del Tredici, 2009; Braak et al., 2003; Masuda-Suzukake et al., 2013; Luk et al., 2009; Desplats et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to experimental studies.

claim: Fetal human midbrain neurons therapeutically implanted into striata of PD patients developed scattered Lewy pathology.
source: Additional evidence for the existence of prion-like mechanisms in the human brain has come from the development of scattered Lewy pathology in fetal human midbrain neurons that were therapeutically implanted into the striata of patients with advanced PD (Kordower et al., 2008; Li et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kordower et al., 2008 and Li et al., 2008.

claim: Transmission of α-syn aggregates from person to person has not been demonstrated.
source: However, unlike canonical prions, transmission of α-syn aggregates from person to person has not been demonstrated, and different polymorphs of aggregated α-syn have not been demonstrated unambiguously in the diseased human brain.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of evidence for person-to-person transmission.

claim: Different polymorphs of aggregated α-syn have not been demonstrated unambiguously in the diseased human brain.
source: However, unlike canonical prions, transmission of α-syn aggregates from person to person has not been demonstrated, and different polymorphs of aggregated α-syn have not been demonstrated unambiguously in the diseased human brain.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of evidence regarding α-syn polymorphs.

claim: The inhibitors were designed using the atomic structure of NACore as a template.
source: Based on the atomic structure of NACore [68-GAVVTGVTAVA-78] as a template, we applied computational and structure-based approaches to design peptidic inhibitors.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: The atomic structure of NACore revealed a pair of self-complementary β-sheets forming a protofilament composed of a homo-steric zipper.
source: The atomic structure of NACore (Rodriguez et al., 2015) revealed a pair of self-complementary β-sheets forming a protofilament composed of a homo-steric zipper (Sawaya et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Rodriguez et al., 2015 and Sawaya et al., 2007.

claim: The inhibitors were designed using Rosetta-based computational modeling to bind to the tip of the steric-zipper protofilament.
source: The inhibitors were designed using Rosetta-based computational modeling to bind to the tip of the steric-zipper protofilament, thereby capping the fibrils (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the computational design methodology and references Figure 1A.

claim: Four candidate inhibitors were identified: S37, S61, S62 and S71.
source: We identified four candidates; S37, S61, S62 and S71 that are computed to bind favorably with one or both ends of the zipper (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the results of the computational design and references Figure 1.

claim: S37, S61, and S62 are predicted to bind to both ends of the NACore protofilament.
source: S37, S61 and S62 are shown here to bind to the end with lower binding energy and S71 is shown to bind the only end to which it is predicted to bind.
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption for Figure 1A and shown in the computational models.

claim: S71 is predicted to bind only to one end of the NACore protofilament.
source: S37, S61 and S62 are shown here to bind to the end with lower binding energy and S71 is shown to bind the only end to which it is predicted to bind.
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption for Figure 1A and shown in the computational models.

claim: S62 binds α-syn fibrils with a Kd of 0.5 μM.
source: The inhibitor S62 showed highest binding affinity towards α-syn fibrils (Kd = 0.5 µM) followed by S61 (Kd = 9.28 µM), S71 (Kd = 10.9 µM) and S37 (Kd = 328 µM) (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from SPR experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: S61 binds α-syn fibrils with a Kd of 9.28 μM.
source: The inhibitor S62 showed highest binding affinity towards α-syn fibrils (Kd = 0.5 µM) followed by S61 (Kd = 9.28 µM), S71 (Kd = 10.9 µM) and S37 (Kd = 328 µM) (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from SPR experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: S71 binds α-syn fibrils with a Kd of 10.9 μM.
source: The inhibitor S62 showed highest binding affinity towards α-syn fibrils (Kd = 0.5 µM) followed by S61 (Kd = 9.28 µM), S71 (Kd = 10.9 µM) and S37 (Kd = 328 µM) (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from SPR experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: S37 binds α-syn fibrils with a Kd of 328 μM.
source: The inhibitor S62 showed highest binding affinity towards α-syn fibrils (Kd = 0.5 µM) followed by S61 (Kd = 9.28 µM), S71 (Kd = 10.9 µM) and S37 (Kd = 328 µM) (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from SPR experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: S61, S62 and S71 showed 6–11-fold lower affinity to α-syn monomers compared to fibrils.
source: S37 bound with similar Kd to both α-syn fibrils and monomers but the improved designs, S61, S62 and S71 showed 6–11-fold lower affinity to α-syn monomers (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on SPR measurements comparing binding to fibrils versus monomers.

claim: All four inhibitors decreased ThT fluorescence indicative of inhibition of aggregation.
source: All four inhibitors decreased ThT fluorescence indicative of inhibition of aggregation.
evidence: This is based on ThT fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: S62 and S61 inhibited α-syn aggregation at equimolar concentrations.
source: S62 and S61 showed most potency and inhibited at equimolar concentrations while S37 and S71 showed efficacy at ten-fold higher concentrations than α-syn.
evidence: This is based on ThT fluorescence assay results.

claim: S37 and S71 showed efficacy at ten-fold higher concentrations than α-syn.
source: S62 and S61 showed most potency and inhibited at equimolar concentrations while S37 and S71 showed efficacy at ten-fold higher concentrations than α-syn.
evidence: This is based on ThT fluorescence assay results.

claim: In the presence of inhibitors, α-syn forms sparse and short fibrils.
source: Electron microscopy (EM) of the aggregated samples confirmed that in the presence of the inhibitors sparse and short fibrils are formed, whereas α-syn aggregated alone forms abundant, long and unbranched fibrils (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 2D.

claim: α-syn aggregated alone forms abundant, long and unbranched fibrils.
source: Electron microscopy (EM) of the aggregated samples confirmed that in the presence of the inhibitors sparse and short fibrils are formed, whereas α-syn aggregated alone forms abundant, long and unbranched fibrils (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Presence of inhibitors results in less abundant, thick bundled fibrils.
source: We also observe that presence of inhibitors results in less abundant, thick bundled fibrils (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Sonicated α-syn fibrils efficiently seed the aggregation of recombinant monomeric α-syn.
source: Aggregation assay showed that short fibrils efficiently seed the aggregation of recombinant monomeric α-syn (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is based on seeded aggregation assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Lipofectamine-mediated transfection of 125 nM recombinant α-syn fibrils seeds the aggregation of endogenous YFP-labeled protein in HEK293 cells.
source: In this model system, lipofectamine-mediated transfection of 125 nM recombinant α-syn fibrils seeds the aggregation of the endogenous YFP-labeled protein, which appear as fluorescent puncta (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This describes the cell culture model system and references supporting figures.

claim: Fluorescent puncta increase in size and number over time in the cell culture model.
source: Additionally, these puncta increase in size and number over time (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, left).
evidence: This is based on time-course observations shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: All four inhibitors showed dose-dependent reduction in puncta in both WT and A53T α-syn expressing cells.
source: We observed a dose-dependent increase in efficacy of all four inhibitors in reducing seeding in both WT and A53T α-syn expressing cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on cell culture seeding assay data shown in Figure 3.

claim: S62 caused significant reduction in puncta when present at equimolar concentrations.
source: S62 caused significant reduction in puncta when present at equimolar concentrations, whereas S61 was effective at 2-fold molar excess or more in both cell lines.
evidence: This is based on cell culture seeding assay results.

claim: S61 was effective at 2-fold molar excess or more in both cell lines.
source: S62 caused significant reduction in puncta when present at equimolar concentrations, whereas S61 was effective at 2-fold molar excess or more in both cell lines.
evidence: This is based on cell culture seeding assay results.

claim: S71 and S37 showed efficacy in reducing cell seeding only at 5- and 10-fold molar excess.
source: S71 and S37 showed efficacy in reducing cell seeding in both cell lines only at 5- and 10-fold molar excess.
evidence: This is based on cell culture seeding assay results.

claim: S62 causes about 25–65-fold decrease in ThT fluorescence of α-syn during aggregation.
source: S62 causes about 25–65-fold decrease in ThT fluorescence of α-syn during aggregation.
evidence: This is based on ThT fluorescence measurements.

claim: S61 causes 8–15-fold decrease in ThT fluorescence compared to 25–65-fold decrease caused by S62.
source: Further, S61 is less potent compared to S62 in inhibiting α-syn aggregation in vitro. S61 causes 8–15-fold decrease in ThT fluorescence compared to 25–65-fold decrease in ThT fluorescence caused by S62 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is based on ThT fluorescence measurements shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: None of the inhibitors showed increase in ThT fluorescence over a period of two days when incubated alone.
source: α-syn used as a positive control showed a time dependent increase in ThT fluorescence indicative of fibril formation but none of the inhibitors showed increase in ThT fluorescence over a period of two days (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on ThT fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: No fibrils were observed in any of the inhibitor samples incubated alone for two days.
source: All samples were also observed by EM (Figure 4B). Abundant fibrils were present in α-syn incubated for two days. No fibrils were observed in any of the inhibitor samples.
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Aggregated inhibitor transfected cells did not have any puncta.
source: The cell culture seeding assay showed that α-syn fibril transfected cells had abundant puncta (shown by white arrows), whereas aggregated inhibitor transfected cells did not have any puncta (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is based on cell culture seeding assay data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Scrambling the binding motif sequence results in loss of inhibitory effect of the designed peptides.
source: This shows that scrambling the binding motif sequence results in loss of inhibitory effect of our designed peptides, and hence that the inhibitor sequence is specific for binding.
evidence: This is based on experiments with scrambled peptide shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: S62 and S61 cause reduction in puncta in both WT and A53T cell lines when co-transfected with pre-formed α-syn fibrils.
source: Two (S62 and S61) out of the four inhibitors cause reduction in puncta in both cell lines (Figure 5B and D).
evidence: This is based on cell culture seeding assay data shown in Figure 5.

claim: 25–100-fold molar excess of inhibitors was required to prevent seeding by pre-formed fibrils in the cell culture assay.
source: Notably, 25–100-fold molar excess of inhibitors was required to prevent seeding by pre-formed fibrils in the cell culture assay (Figure 5) as opposed to maximum 10-fold molar excess in case of cell seeding with α-syn aggregated in presence of inhibitors (Figure 3).
evidence: This is based on comparison of cell culture seeding assay results shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: Incubation of pre-formed α-syn fibrils with inhibitors S62 and S61 results in bundling of fibrils into thick morphologies.
source: Incubation of pre-formed α-syn fibrils with inhibitors S62 and S61 results in lateral association of fibrils to form thick, bundled morphologies (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Inhibitors S71 and S37 do not affect the morphology of α-syn fibrils.
source: On the other hand, the inhibitors S71 and S37, which do not significantly affect cell seeding ability of α-syn fibrils do not affect the morphology of α-syn fibrils (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: α-syn is present in extracts from both MSA brain samples and the control brain sample.
source: Western blot analysis using α-syn-specific antibody showed that α-syn is present in extracts from both MSA brain samples and the control brain sample (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is based on Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Fibrillar structures were found in extracts from both MSA samples but not in control brain extracts.
source: EM analysis of these extracts showed fibrillar structures in extracts from both MSA samples, whereas no fibril-like structures were found in control brain extracts (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Robust seeding was observed in HEK293 cells expressing A53T α-syn seven days after transfection with extracts from MSA brain samples.
source: We observed robust seeding in HEK293 cells expressing A53T α-syn seven days after transfection with extracts from each of the MSA brain samples but low levels of seeding in WT α-syn expressing HEK293 cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2 and 6D).
evidence: This is based on cell culture seeding assay data shown in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Transfection with buffer or extracts from control brain samples does not cause seeding in cells.
source: Transfection with buffer or extracts from control brain samples does not cause seeding in cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on cell culture seeding assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: All four inhibitors significantly reduce cell seeding by both MSA1 and MSA2 samples.
source: All four inhibitors significantly reduce cell seeding by both MSA1 and MSA2 samples (Figure 7B, C, D and E).
evidence: This is based on cell culture seeding assay data shown in Figure 7.

claim: S62 was the most potent inhibitor against MSA-derived α-syn fibrils followed by S71, S37 and S61.
source: Quantification of puncta formed in each condition showed that S62 was the most potent inhibitor followed by S71, S37 and S61 (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is based on quantification of cell culture seeding assay data shown in Figure 7D and E.

claim: The inhibitors prevent α-syn aggregation in vitro with binding affinities of 0.5 μM to α-syn fibril seeds.
source: The inhibitors prevent α-syn aggregation in vitro and in cell culture models with binding affinities of 0.5 μM to α-syn fibril seeds.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by SPR data in the results.

claim: The inhibitors show efficacy in preventing seeding by human patient-derived α-syn fibrils.
source: The inhibitors also show efficacy in preventing seeding by human patient-derived α-syn fibrils.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by MSA patient-derived fibril experiments.

claim: Pathogenic seeds of α-syn contain steric zippers.
source: Our results suggest that pathogenic seeds of α-syn contain steric zippers and suggest a therapeutic approach targeted at the spread and progression that may be applicable for PD and related synucleinopathies.
evidence: This is an inference based on the efficacy of inhibitors designed to target steric zippers.

claim: Nearly 100 different designs were tested experimentally using in vitro aggregation assays with sequential rounds of optimization.
source: To find the most effective inhibitors, nearly 100 different designs were tested experimentally using in vitro aggregation assays with sequential rounds of optimization on the inhibitor design.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: The location of the tag on N- or C- terminus affects the efficacy of the inhibitors.
source: For example, we observed that the location of the tag on N- or C- terminus affects the efficacy of the inhibitors.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental optimization process.

claim: Only a Trp substitution at Thr72 was effective whereas Arg substitution was not.
source: Additionally, the type of modification added can also affect its efficacy. In our case, only a Trp substitution at Thr72 was effective whereas Arg substitution was not.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental optimization process.

claim: S37, S61 and S62 retain the same binding motif/inhibitor sequence but show variability in their binding affinities towards recombinant α-syn fibrils.
source: Notably, S37, S61 and S62 retain the same binding motif/inhibitor sequence but show variability in their binding affinities towards recombinant α-syn fibrils as well as their potencies in inhibiting α-syn aggregation in vitro.
evidence: This is based on comparison of SPR and aggregation assay data for the three inhibitors.

claim: α-syn fibrils can seed only α-syn protein into aggregates and not other amyloid-forming proteins such as Tau and amyloid-β.
source: For example, α-syn fibrils can seed only α-syn protein into aggregates and not other amyloid-forming proteins such as Tau and amyloid-β (Sanders et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Sanders et al., 2014.

claim: No acute cell death was observed upon formation of puncta in the cell culture system.
source: Notably, in this system we do not observe acute cell death upon formation of puncta (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, right).
evidence: This is based on cell growth measurements shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: A single administration of inhibitors is effective up to 7 days in the cell culture system.
source: Our inhibitors prevent puncta formation in this system with a single administration of inhibitors being effective up to 7 days.
evidence: This is based on the MSA patient-derived fibril experiments where cells were imaged 7 days after transfection.

claim: Fibrils formed by the A53T familial mutant protein are structurally similar to WT fibrils.
source: Fibrils formed by the A53T familial mutant protein are structurally similar to WT fibrils and can be inhibited by the peptidic inhibitors.
evidence: This is inferred from the efficacy of inhibitors in both WT and A53T cell lines.

claim: The A53T mutation increases the aggregation propensity of α-syn.
source: Among the seven presently known missense familial mutations associated with PD, we chose A53T because it has been shown to increase the aggregation propensity of α-syn (Flagmeier et al., 2016; Li et al., 2001; Narhi et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Flagmeier et al., 2016; Li et al., 2001; Narhi et al., 1999.

claim: MSA patient-extracted α-syn fibrils cause abundant puncta formation in the cell culture model.
source: We observe that MSA patient-extracted α-syn fibrils cause abundant puncta formation in our cell culture model.
evidence: This is based on cell culture seeding assay data with MSA patient-derived fibrils.

claim: A53T α-syn has higher propensity to form fibrils than WT α-syn.
source: Since A53T α-syn has higher propensity to form fibrils, we observe more aggressive seeding by MSA patient-extracted α-syn fibrils in A53T α-syn expressing HEK cells compared to WT α-syn expressing HEK cells.
evidence: This is based on comparison of seeding in WT versus A53T cell lines and supported by literature citations.

claim: Inhibitors targeted against Tau show efficacy at 25–100-fold molar excess concentrations.
source: Incidentally, inhibitors targeted against Tau, an Alzheimer's -associated amyloid protein also show efficacy at 25–100-fold molar excess concentrations (Seidler et al., 2018) suggesting that secondary nucleation is a common mechanism of aggregation of amyloid proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Seidler et al., 2018.

claim: Secondary nucleation is a common mechanism of aggregation of amyloid proteins.
source: Incidentally, inhibitors targeted against Tau, an Alzheimer's -associated amyloid protein also show efficacy at 25–100-fold molar excess concentrations (Seidler et al., 2018) suggesting that secondary nucleation is a common mechanism of aggregation of amyloid proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison with Tau inhibitors and the high concentrations required for efficacy.

claim: The inhibitors can be used as a diagnostic to identify different α-syn strains.
source: Our inhibitors can also be used as a diagnostic to identify different α-syn strains.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on the differential efficacy of inhibitors.

claim: A cocktail of different inhibitors targeting different polymorphs might be effective in the absence of a diagnostic.
source: In the absence of a diagnostic, a cocktail of different inhibitors targeting different polymorphs might be effective.
evidence: This is a speculative therapeutic suggestion.

claim: Computational designs were done using the FastDesign protocol in Rosetta version 3.8.
source: Computational designs were done using the FastDesign protocol in Rosetta version 3.8, according to previously described methods (Sievers et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the computational methodology and cites Sievers et al., 2011.

claim: The crystal structure of NACore (PDB ID: 4RIL) was used as a design template.
source: Briefly, the crystal structure of the NACore segment (PDB ID: 4RIL) was used as a design template.
evidence: This describes the structural template used for computational design.

claim: The α-syn construct was transformed into Escherichia coli expression cell line BL21 (DE3) gold.
source: The α-syn construct was transformed into Escherichia coli expression cell line BL21 (DE3) gold (Agilent Technologies).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology for protein expression.

claim: The peptide inhibitors were commercially obtained from Genscript Inc at greater than 98% purity.
source: The peptide inhibitors were commercially obtained from Genscript Inc at greater than 98% purity.
evidence: This describes the source and purity of the inhibitors.

claim: HEK293 cells that stably express YFP labeled WT α-syn and A53T α-syn were a gift from Dr. Marc Diamond.
source: HEK293 cells that stably express YFP labeled WT α-syn and A53T α-syn were a generous gift from Dr. Marc Diamond.
evidence: This describes the source of the cell lines used in the study.

claim: The cell line was generated and validated in Sanders et al. (2014).
source: Cell line was generated and validated in Sanders et al. (2014) and no additional validation was performed.
evidence: This cites the original source of the cell line validation.

claim: Frozen brain tissue samples were obtained from UCLA Brain Tumor Translational Resource (BTTR) and The Human Brain and Spinal Fluid Resource Center (NIH Neurobiobank).
source: Frozen brain tissue samples from two different MSA subjects and one age-matched control subject were obtained from UCLA Brain Tumor Translational Resource (BTTR) and The Human Brain and Spinal Fluid Resource Center (NIH Neurobiobank).
evidence: This describes the source of human tissue samples.

claim: Insoluble protein aggregates were extracted using a protocol that included precipitation with phosphotungstate anion (PTA) and the ionic detergent sarkosyl.
source: From the frozen brain tissue samples we extracted insoluble protein aggregates using previously published protocol that included precipitation with Phosphotungstate anion (PTA) and the ionic detergent sarkosyl (Woerman et al., 2015; Prusiner et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the extraction methodology and cites Woerman et al., 2015 and Prusiner et al., 2015.
